metadata.original_text: This time series records cheese USD Lbs data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2026-03-06 to 2026-03-23. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The Global Dairy Trade (GDT) auction held on March 3 recorded a 5.7% overall increase in its price index, driven largely by milk powders. During the same auction, cheddar cheese prices also saw a positive lift, rising by 4.3% (approximately 4.5%) to an average of US$4,920/MT. <2> On February 1, 2026, the Milk Market Administrator for the Appalachian and Southeast Marketing Areas (Federal Orders 5 and 7) issued a market update for February 2026. The update included the latest news and announcements, such as details regarding the Transportation Credit Balancing Fund, and officially reported a $0.03 per pound increase in the monthly cheese commodity price factored into regional formulas. <3> Economists from the National Milk Producers Federation (NMPF), including Will Loux and Stephen Cain, reported that U.S. cheese prices had been suppressed in the $1.50 to $1.60 range. They noted that this price stagnation was largely driven by strong international competition and abundant milk and cheese supplies from Europe. This kept U.S. prices at parity with European markets, despite steady and robust domestic production, which saw U.S. cheese supply increase by 2.9% in 2025. <4> Industry advisory firm MilkPay published a 2026 dairy pricing projection, forecasting that U.S. cheese prices will likely remain stable at current levels or experience a slight decline throughout the year. The report, attributes this expected price stability to a balance between robust domestic cheese production—which is currently outpacing domestic consumption—and increasing, record-high export volumes driven by competitive pricing. <5> During the Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 397 held on February 3, 2026, the overall dairy price index surged by 6.7%, largely driven by a 10.6% spike in skim milk powder prices. This global rally, however, highlighted a significant divergence in the U.S. market. Domestic cheese futures (Class III contracts) severely lagged behind the soaring global powder and fat prices (Class IV contracts). This discrepancy is driven by a localized cheese oversupply in the U.S., stemming from massive investments in processing plants during 2024 and 2025 that have flooded the market with cheese blocks and barrels, keeping spot prices depressed despite global commodity gains. <6> Market reports indicated that CME block cheese prices increased by $0.03 to $1.38 per pound, and barrels rose by $0.05 to $1.41 per pound. These market shifts were supported by steady U.S. production and improving export demand. <7> The USDA released its December 2025 Cold Storage report, revealing that natural cheese stocks as of December 31, 2025, rose to 1.35 billion pounds. This represented a one percent increase over both November 2025 and December 2024 figures, highlighting a continued national inventory surplus of cheese. <8> The Vesper Price Index reported that large production surpluses in the United States, driven by herd sizes reaching their highest levels since the 1990s and a nearly 3 percent year-over-year increase in February production, pressured American Mozzarella and other protein-based product prices downward by 15 percent to €2,575/mt. This price drop created a significant discount compared to European offerings, successfully securing necessary export volumes. Consequently, U.S. cheese exports surged 29 percent year-over-year due to strong competitiveness in contested markets such as Japan and South Korea. Looking ahead, the USDA forecasts that U.S. cheese exports will continue to rise by about 3 percent from 2025, supported by expanding processing capacity, competitive pricing, and robust international demand. <9> The USDA Food and Nutrition Service has officially updated its processor material price valuations for School Year 2026 to be used on the Summary End Product Data Schedules (SEPDS). To provide stable valuations in a volatile market and facilitate the rebating or discounting of finished product prices for school food programs, the 24-month weighted average price was set at $1.8444 per pound for mozzarella and $1.9915 per pound for all other cheeses. <10> An industry report published on November 26, 2025, highlighted that U.S. cheese exports achieved record highs, surging 14.1% year-to-date. This growth was driven by a distinct global price advantage, with CME block Cheddar averaging $1.85 per pound over the preceding 12 months, significantly undercutting European Cheddar at $2.34 and New Zealand Cheddar at $2.20 per pound.
